newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan share prices close at new 1996 high.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan share prices close at new 1996 high.

text.p: Taiwan share prices pushed to a 1996 closing high on Wednesday, warding off late profit-taking pressure on strong buying in the island's bedrock financial and electronics shares, brokers said.
The weighted index closed 49.51 points or 0.75 percent higher at 6,653.65, besting the previous year high of 6,644.66 set on October 5. Turnover was a hectic T$67.01 billion.

The market, buoyed by government decisions to free one major state fund to invest in stocks and loosen the investment cap for another, has risen nearly 300 points in the last six sessions after a long slump in October.
The market largely ignored the re-election of U.S. president Bill Clinton, which became apparent during trading.
"The result was pretty much expected, and even if it weren't the market would not have a clear reaction to it," said Lin Long-hsien, securities analyst for United Securities.
Brokers expected late profit-taking but blue-chip financial and electronic shares easily overcame the selling pressure.

"Some investors wanted to take advantage of the recent bull run to take the index to a new level, so they concentrated buying on the two sectors most likely to affect overall market -- electronics and financials," said Lin.
Financial shares ended 1.36 percent higher, with China Life Insurance soaring the daily seven percent limit or T$4 to T$67 and Cathay Life Insurance gaining T$2 to T$171.
Electronics shares, which have paced the market in recent weeks on sound earnings reports, closed 1.15 percent higher. D-Link Corp also finished limit-up, gaining T$3.50 at T$55.50.
Brokers expected the market to continue testing a higher upside. A 6,620-6,700 range was seen for Thursday.
